newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY BCE MILLING WHEAT MIXED, BARLEY DOWN.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY BCE MILLING WHEAT MIXED, BARLEY DOWN.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices were mixed on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Tuesday as large sales pushed some maturities lower, traders said.
"One brokerage was selling large amounts of milling wheat," said Tamas Kobulniczky of Swap brokerage.
He added that the rest of the market was puzzled by the move and that even these sales could not achieve an across-the-board drop in milling wheat prices.
"This shows the extent of the (milling) wheat shortage," Kobulniczky said.
September milling wheat rose 270 forints per tonne to 28,370, October dropped 930 to 29,400, December finished 560 forints lower at 30,810 but January jumped 920 forints to 31,120.
Maturities from March 1998 onward finished steady to lower.

Feed barley prices dropped the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all but the nearest maturity, September, to finish between 20,600 for October and 22,300 for May, but Kobulniczky said the minimal turnover showed prices were not necessarily indicative of any trend.
"Feed barley keeps moving up and down in a fairly steady range," he said.
Feed wheat futures eased 100 forints for September and were steady for May but rose by 50 to 400 forints for all other maturities.
Kobulniczky said that although everybody expected the market to be flooded with feed wheat, prices had to bottom out.
"It may be true that there is a lot of feed wheat, but it still has some value," he said.
He also said maize futures, which finished lower for all but the two most remote maturities, November and December 1998, were undervalued.
"Maize is irrationally cheap," Kobulniczky said. There were reasonably good chances for exports to neighbouring countries and export prices would sooner or later give support to BCE maize prices.
Maize futures finished at 18,100 forints for September, 18,300 for December and 21,380 for July.
Total grains futures turnover was a mediocre 1,397 lots or 769.3 million forints, virtually unchanged from Monday's 1,334 lots or 766.8 million forints.
